sights.address: 135 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The modernist 1960s presidential palace where NVA Tank 843 crashed the gate on 30 April 1975, ending the war. Frozen-in-time state rooms, war-command bunker and telecoms basement. National monument; daily ~07:00-18:00, 80,000d.

sights.address: 01 Cong xa Paris, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The twin-spired red-brick French cathedral (1863-1880) built with imported Marseille materials, on the square opposite the Post Office. UNDER RESTORATION since 2017 (interior closed to visitors; completion pushed to ~2027, scaffolding coming off by early 2026) — view the exterior.

sights.address: 125 Cong xa Paris (Hai Ba Trung), Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: Working 1886-1891 post office (architect Alfred Foulhoux; often mis-credited to Eiffel) with a vaulted iron-truss hall, painted maps and a portrait of Ho Chi Minh. Ranked among the world's most beautiful post offices; still operational.

sights.address: 73 Mai Thi Luu, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: Saigon's most atmospheric Taoist temple, built by the Cantonese community in 1909, thick with incense smoke and carved wooden deities incl. the Hall of Ten Hells and a turtle pond. Obama visited in 2016. Free, ~07:00-18:00.

sights.n: Nguyen Hue Walking Street & People's Committee Building
sights.address: Nguyen Hue Boulevard, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The city's 900 m pedestrian boulevard (a former canal, walkerised 2015) running from the floodlit French Hotel de Ville / People's Committee Building (1898-1909, viewed from outside) and Ho Chi Minh statue down to the Saigon River. Liveliest at night.

sights.address: 07 Cong Truong Lam Son, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: Flamboyant 1897-1900 French Beaux-Arts theatre, once seat of South Vietnam's Lower House, now a national relic staging the acclaimed bamboo-circus A O Show and The Mist.

sights.address: 36 Ho Tung Mau, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The 262 m lotus-bud tower (2010) with a helipad wing and the 49th-floor Saigon Skydeck, the city's first observation deck, giving 360-degree views over the river. Open daily ~09:30-21:30.

sights.n: Ho Chi Minh City Museum (Gia Long Palace)
sights.address: 65 Ly Tu Trong, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: City-history museum in an 1885-1890 neoclassical palace that served the French governor, President Diem (as Gia Long Palace) and the RVN Supreme Court, with a wartime bunker/tunnel beneath. Traces Saigon from prehistory to reunification.

sights.address: 2 Nguyen Binh Khiem, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: Vietnam's national-history collection in a 1926-1929 Indochinese-style building beside the Botanical Gardens: Cham and Oc Eo antiquities, Dong Son drums, a mummified noblewoman, plus water-puppet shows. Closed Mondays.

sights.n: Fine Arts Museum (Bao tang My thuat)
sights.address: 97A Pho Duc Chinh, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The city's leading art museum in a yellow 1929-1934 Franco-Chinese mansion of the wealthy Hua family, with the first lift in Saigon; holds lacquer, silk and war-era painting plus Champa/Oc Eo relics. Closed Mondays.

sights.address: 42 Nguyen Hue, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A crumbling 1960s nine-storey block (once housing for US advisers) reborn as a vertical warren of independent cafes, boutiques and bars, each balcony overlooking the walking street. Slow lift ~3,000d, or take the stairs.

sights.n: Book Street (Duong Sach Nguyen Van Binh)
sights.address: Nguyen Van Binh, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A shaded 144 m pedestrian lane beside the cathedral and Post Office lined with 20-plus publisher stalls, secondhand-book stands and book cafes, plus author events. Free; best in the evening.

sights.address: Bui Vien Street, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: Saigon's neon backpacker strip in the Pham Ngu Lao quarter (on the map since Lonely Planet's 1993 guide) — bar stools spilling into the road, street food and live music. Pedestrianised nightly; peaks Fri-Sun.

sights.n: Ho Chi Minh Museum - Dragon House Wharf (Nha Rong)
sights.address: 1 Nguyen Tat Thanh, District 4, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The 1862-1863 twin-dragon-roofed former Messageries Maritimes house on the riverfront from which the 21-year-old future Ho Chi Minh sailed to France in June 1911; a branch of the Ho Chi Minh Museum since 1979. Closed Mondays.

sights.address: Cong Truong Quoc Te (Pham Ngoc Thach / Tran Cao Van), District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A modernist 1967-1972 traffic-circle monument of five splayed concrete 'hands' and an octagonal fountain, on the site of a French water tower and an old Nguyen-era citadel gate. Now a beloved evening hangout for street snacks.

sights.address: 202 Vo Thi Sau, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A 31,000-object museum (est. 1985; Class-I museum from 2024) devoted to southern Vietnamese women in war and culture — female guerrillas, ao dai history and Mother Goddess worship. Closed Mondays; free.

sights.address: 5 Ton Duc Thang, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: Riverside museum (opened 1988) to Ton Duc Thang, Vietnam's second president and a Con Dao political prisoner, with 16,000+ documents on his life and the labour movement. Closed Mondays; free.

sights.address: 104 Yersin, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The 'American Market' off Yersin St, famous since 1975 for army-surplus gear, dog tags, ponchos and militaria (genuine and replica) alongside hardware stalls — a gritty relic of the war years. Bargain and check provenance.

sights.address: 339 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia, Ward 7, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The city's largest Mahayana pagoda (built 1964-1971 with Japanese aid), the first to render traditional temple form in concrete, crowned by a seven-storey, 40 m stupa. Free.

sights.address: 89 Ba Huyen Thanh Quan, Vo Thi Sau Ward, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A seven-storey 1956-1958 pagoda that was the flashpoint of the 1963 Buddhist Crisis: the epicentre of anti-Diem protests and the 21 August 1963 army raid that arrested hundreds of monks and helped trigger the coup.

sights.address: 289 Hai Ba Trung, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The bubblegum-pink Romano-Gothic Catholic church begun 1870-1876 (its signature pink dates to a 1957 repaint) — the city's second-largest church and a landmark photo stop. Active parish; exterior always, interior around Mass times.

sights.address: 720A Dien Bien Phu, Ward 22, Binh Thanh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: At 461 m the tallest building in Vietnam (2018), a bamboo-cluster supertall over the Saigon River in Vinhomes Central Park. The SkyView observatory spans floors 79-81 for the city's highest panorama.

sights.address: 710 Nguyen Trai, Ward 11, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: Cholon's most famous temple (Tue Thanh Guildhall), built by Cantonese immigrants around 1760 for Mazu, sea goddess of the overseas Chinese. Famed for its porcelain-figurine roof friezes and hanging incense coils. National monument.

sights.address: 57A Thap Muoi, Ward 2, District 6 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: Cholon's grand wholesale market, financed by merchant Quach Dam and completed 1928, built around a pagoda-roofed courtyard; a recognised heritage building (restored 2016-2018) and still a major distribution hub.

sights.address: 25 Hoc Lac, Ward 14, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: Cholon's Chinese-Catholic parish church (1900-1902), Gothic with Chinese detailing. Here President Ngo Dinh Diem and his brother took refuge and surrendered during the 1 November 1963 coup, before being killed en route.

sights.address: 678 Nguyen Trai, Ward 11, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A 19th-century Teochew guildhall temple to the deified warlord Quan Cong, one of Cholon's oldest, celebrated for its gilded woodwork, a huge red-lacquer horse of Quan Cong and intricate roof ceramics.

sights.address: 264 Hai Thuong Lan Ong, Ward 14, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A Fujianese assembly-hall temple (Nhi Phu Hoi Quan, from the late 17th/18th c.) venerating Ong Bon, guardian god of land and wealth; ship-prow roofs, carved red pillars and a national relic listing (1998).

sights.address: 802 Nguyen Trai, Ward 14, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A southern-Fujian (Zhangzhou) guildhall temple founded 1809 for Thien Hau, with four China-carved dragon-wrapped stone pillars shipped in by boat and vivid ceramic roof scenes; especially alive at the Lantern Festival.

sights.address: 565 Lac Long Quan, Ward 10, Tan Binh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: Believed the oldest temple in the city (founded 1744), atmospheric in garden grounds with a Bodhi tree, a nine-tier stupa and thousands of decorative plates set into its walls. National relic. Free.

sights.address: Long Hoa, Hoa Thanh, Tay Ninh Province, Vietnam (day trip ~90 km NW of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
sights.w: The kaleidoscopic 1933-1955 Great Temple of Caodaism, Vietnam's homegrown syncretic religion, with a divine 'all-seeing eye', dragon pillars and rainbow interior. Time a visit for the white-robed noon ceremony. Often paired with Cu Chi.

sights.n: Mekong Delta Day Trip (My Tho & Ben Tre)
sights.address: My Tho (Tien Giang) & Ben Tre Provinces, Vietnam (day trip ~70-90 km SW of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
sights.w: The classic close Delta day trip: a Tien River cruise past the Dragon/Unicorn/Phoenix/Tortoise islets, sampan rides through coconut-palm canals, a coconut-candy workshop, honey tea and the large Vinh Trang Pagoda at My Tho.

sights.address: Ninh Son, Tay Ninh Province, Vietnam (day trip ~100 km NW of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
sights.w: The 986 m 'Black Virgin Mountain', highest peak in the south, a pilgrimage site of cave temples reached by a Guinness-record cable-car system to Sun World, with a 72 m bronze Bodhisattva at the summit. Pairs with Tay Ninh's Cao Dai temple.

sights.n: Can Gio Mangrove Biosphere Reserve (Monkey Island)
sights.address: Can Gio District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (~50-60 km SE of the centre)
sights.w: Vietnam's first UNESCO Man-and-Biosphere reserve (designated 2000), a replanted mangrove forest that was the Viet Cong's Rung Sac guerrilla zone. Boat trips, a reconstructed guerrilla base, crocodile lagoons and a large troop of macaques ('Monkey Island').

sights.address: Cai Rang District, Can Tho, Mekong Delta, Vietnam (long day trip / overnight ~170 km SW of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
sights.w: The biggest floating wholesale market in the Delta, where boats trade produce hung from tall poles at dawn on the Can Tho River. Deep in the Delta (~3.5 hrs each way) — best as an early-start long day trip or overnight; trades wind down by ~08:30.

sights.address: Ha Long St, Ward 2, Vung Tau, Ba Ria-Vung Tau Province, Vietnam (day trip ~95 km / 2-hr ferry from Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
sights.w: The nearest beach escape: a seaside town crowned by a 32 m Christ the King statue (1974) you can climb (~800 steps inside) for coastal views, plus the White Palace and Back Beach. Reachable by road or Saigon River fast ferry.
